posts.title: macOS 27 Activates Mission Control when Dragging Files to Zight Menu Bar App
posts.description: Since upgrading to macOS 27, dragging a file to the Zight menu bar item (to upload it) would trigger Mission Control. This got super annoying, and no settings stuff seems to have really done anything to fix it. Even the one that is called "Drag windows to top of screen to enter Mission Control" didn't stop this, because I was dragging a file not a window. (It did turn off dragging windows to the top triggering Mission Control, as it says.) So… defaults write com.apple.dock enterMissionControlByTopWindowDrag -bool false;killall Dock Somehow, that seems to resolve the issue, but it's strange because it's just toggling the same thing as in the System Settings. Edit a few hours later: It worked for awhile, then stopped. So, scratch that. The best work-around I've found is to open the Zight window/menu, and drop items onto that as it's well below/away from the menu bar. P.S. Dragging windows to the title bar does not bring up Mission Control. Dragging files does. Grrrrr.

posts.title: R.E.M. Chicago-Area Concerts from the 80s
posts.description: Aadam Jacobs , sometimes called Chicago Tape Guy, is a concertgoer and archivist in Chicago, Illinois, known for recording more than 10,000 tapes of indie and punk rock concerts between 1984 and the 2010s. Described as a "ubiquitous local club presence" and "rabid fan" by the Chicago Tribune,[1] Jacobs captured an estimated 30,000 music sets from at least 3000 music acts[2] including R.E.M., The Cure, Tracy Chapman, Depeche Mode, Sonic Youth, and Nirvana.[3] Since late 2024, dozens of volunteers have digitized, cataloged, and published thousands of his audio files. That effort is here: https://aadamjacobs.dunlap.ai . Wow! I spent the morning getting work done while listening to an R.E.M. concert from 1986. Amazing.
